subject: Payment API: p95/p99 latency spike + 429 retry-wave (Clearpath)
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@clearpath.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Rivera <marco.rivera@clearpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 20:58:00 +0000
Subject: [Urgent] Checkout failures + p99 spikes since 20:40Z

Hi Markus / Marissa,

We started seeing elevated p95/p99 latencies and a surge of 429s against the Redwood hosted Payment API around 20:40Z. Our checkout requests are timing out or retrying and it’s causing a backlog of in‑flight payments. We’ve already seen a ~12% failure rate on checkouts in the last 20 minutes.

Attached is a 15m p95 heatmap and a short snippet of our client retry logs. Quick observations from our side:
- 429s spike coincides with a burst of parallel retries from multiple edge instances.
- Client backoff is exponential but with minimal jitter—many retries line up.
- Timeouts start surfacing as service calls queue up after the 429s.

We need an immediate mitigation — can you tell us if you can temporarily raise burst limits for our tenant or apply a prioritized path? We’re in mid‑deployment for a major payment push and this is consumer facing.

Attached: p95-heatmap-20270424.png, request-logs-clearpath-20270424.jsonl

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Lee
SRE, Clearpath AI
[susan.lee@clearpath.ai]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 21:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Checkout failures + p99 spikes since 20:40Z

Thanks for the signal, Susan — we see the same pattern on our telemetry. Looping in Eng/Infra.

Immediate actions we’re taking now:
- Ops: opening a short burst window for Clearpath (10m capacity bump) while we triage.
- Eng: isolating request fanout patterns and checking whether tenant‑level rate limiter is triggering cascade retries.
- Ask to Clearpath: can your team push a quick client config change to add ~200–400ms jitter to retries? That will help de‑synchronize retries while we patch.

Rishi — please triage queueing, KV cache pressure, and whether a hot path in the hosted runtime is thrashing under retry amplification. Marissa, I’ll keep customer comms current.

Attachment: internal-hotfix-plan-rollback.md (draft)

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 21:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Checkout failures + p99 spikes since 20:40Z

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Root symptom appears to be retry amplification against tenant API keys. The per-tenant rate limiter responded to a short burst, returning 429s. Clients with aggressive retry loops re‑issued requests in waves, generating further 429s and causing queueing on the hosted frontends.
- Observed phenomenon: tail latency growth as frontends spent cycles decoding/validating now‑stale requests while downstreams had hot KV cache churn (cache misses from repeated new contexts).
- P95/P99 heatmap (linked) shows two concentrated windows at 20:37–20:44Z and 20:52–20:56Z matching client retry waves.

Proposed immediate mitigations (safest first):
1) Ops: Extend temporary burst capacity for Clearpath for +30m (we already did a short 10m bump).
2) Runtime patch (hotfix): throttle per-connection in‑flight requests to 6 and enable server‑side retry‑jitter window (randomized 100–400ms). This prevents simultaneous retry bursts aligning. Can ship in a ~20‑30m canary.
3) Rate limiter change: add a fast fail path for requests with known retry loops (detect via rapid replays from same client ip/key) to return 429 + Retry-After with longer backoff header.
4) Customer guidance: ask Clearpath to roll out client jitter change (200–400ms) immediately.

I’ll prepare a minimal canary that only affects Clearpath traffic so we can measure impact quickly. If we see queue depth reduce and p99 trend down, we can widen.

Metrics:
- Peak 429 rate for tenant: 1,900/min at 20:42Z
- Frontend queue depth spike: 6→48 in 90s (per frontend shard)
- KV miss rate +60% across serving nodes during burst

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

- Approval to extend burst to 30m and authorise extra GPU pool on standby (cost centre: Sales-EMER).
- Guidance on customer comms: short note acknowledging impact + what we’re doing (no blame).
- If the canary reduces p99, we’ll widen; if not, we should consider traffic diversion to dedicated pool for Clearpath.
